name: MA-06
label: Safe D

key_factors: District leans Democratic by eleven points and has consistently elected Democrats
Dan Koh holds a roughly nine-to-one fundraising edge over Micah Jones, plus $1.8 million in outside support with no Republican outside spending
Prediction markets price Democratic odds near 97 percent
Open seat after Seth Moulton's retirement, but no polling suggests competition
model.rationale: The district's eleven-point Democratic lean, Koh's roughly nine-to-one fundraising advantage, and outside support with no Republican counter-spending point to a comfortable Democratic hold of this open seat, and prediction markets agree at about 97 percent.
model.watch: Any late polling showing a single-digit race or a surge of Republican outside spending would justify moving the rating toward Likely D.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Seth Moulton (D) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Massachusetts' Sixth District leans Democratic by eleven points, and the open-seat contest to replace Seth Moulton has developed into a heavily one-sided race. Dan Koh has raised more than $5.2 million, holds about $1 million in cash, and benefits from roughly $1.8 million in outside support, while Republican Micah Jones has raised under $600,000 with no recorded outside spending. Prediction markets price Democratic odds near 97 percent.

No public general-election polls are available, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, the money gap, and a favorable national environment for Democrats. The seat has been held by Democrats, and Moulton's retirement does little to change the underlying partisan advantage. The forecast expects Koh to win by roughly twenty points, with the main uncertainty coming from the absence of polling rather than any sign of a competitive race.
